sections.text: On Gmail on a computer: Go to Gmail on your computer. On the left, click 'More', then 'Trash'. Check the box to the left of each message you want to recover. At the top, click 'Move to'. In the 'Move to' menu, choose the folder where you want the messages to go, such as your inbox. When you delete a message in Gmail, it's moved to Trash. Up to 30 days after deletion, you can find the message in Trash. After 30 days, the message is permanently deleted and can't be recovered. Deleted drafts can't be recovered from Trash.

On Outlook.com: Open the Deleted Items folder and check whether the message is there. If it is, select the message and select 'Restore'. If the message isn't in Deleted Items, open that folder. Above the message list, select 'Recover items deleted from this folder'. If you find the message, select it and then select 'Restore'. Messages removed from the Deleted Items folder are recoverable for 30 days.

sections.text: On Gmail on a computer: On your computer, open Gmail. Review the sender's messages before unsubscribing. In the left menu, click 'More', then 'Manage subscriptions'. On the right, next to the number of recent emails from that sender, click 'Unsubscribe'. Gmail unsubscribes you from all active mailing lists related to the sender. The sender may take a few days to process the request, so you may still receive emails during that time. New emails from the unsubscribed sender go to Spam, with a banner explaining why. Some senders send you to their website. If a pop-up appears, click 'Go to website' to unsubscribe there, or 'Block instead' to block the sender. Blocking a sender does not unsubscribe you from their mailing list. Their future emails go directly to Spam. The ability to manage email subscriptions is gradually rolling out and may not be available to you yet.
